    Lab 3c: Focal Mechanism Inversion¶

    In this lab, you will learn how to:

    • Perform grid search in strike–dip–rake (SDR) space to fit observed polarity and S/P amplitude ratios
    • Use four types of inputs: station polarity, station S/P amplitude ratio, DAS polarity, and DAS S/P amplitude ratio
    • Explore seven inversion modes combining the four types of inputs
    • Identify stable solutions using hierarchical clustering
    • Evaluate solution quality (A/B/C/D) based on misfit and uncertainty

    References:

    • Hardebeck, J. L., & Shearer, P. M. (2002). A new method for determining first-motion focal mechanisms. Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America, 92(6), 2264–2276.

    • Luo, B., Jin, G., & Stanek, F. (2021). Near-field strain in distributed acoustic sensing-based microseismic observation. Geophysics, 86(5), P49-P60. (DAS strain-rate theory)

    • Li, J., Zhu, W., Biondi, E., & Zhan, Z. (2023). Earthquake focal mechanisms with distributed acoustic sensing. Nature Communications, 14, 4181.

    • Skoumal, R. J., Hardebeck, J. L., & Shearer, P. M. (2024). SKHASH: A Python package for computing earthquake focal mechanisms. Seismological Research Letters, 95(4), 2519–2526.

    1. Determing Input Data and Inversion Modes¶

    Our inversion package uses both polarity and S/P amplitude ratio measurements from conventional stations and DAS arrays, providing complementary constraints on the focal mechanism.

    Four Input Data Types¶

    Data type Source Description
    sta_pol Conventional stations P-wave first-motion polarity (±1), manually or auto-picked
    sta_sp Conventional stations S/P amplitude ratio (log₁₀), from broadband seismograms
    das_pol DAS fiber P-wave polarity extracted via MCCC cross-correlation + SVD (lab 3b)
    das_sp DAS fiber S/P amplitude ratio (log₁₀), from windowed DAS strain-rate data (lab 3b)

    Seven Inversion Modes¶

    Different data types can be combined to define inversion modes. Here, we select seven representative modes from all possible combinations.

    # Data uesed Internal name Solver
    1 sta_pol STA_pol pol-only
    2 sta_pol + sta_sp STA_pol_sp joint
    3 das_pol DAS_pol pol-only
    4 das_pol + das_sp DAS_pol_sp joint
    5 sta_pol + das_pol STA_pol_DAS_pol pol-only
    6 sta_pol + das_sp STA_pol_DAS_sp joint
    7 sta_pol + das_pol + das_sp STA_pol_DAS_pol_sp joint

    Two solver types are used depending on whether S/P ratios are included:

    • Polarity-only — grid search minimizes polarity misfit (fraction of sign disagreements)
    • Joint (pol + S/P) — grid search minimizes combined polarity misfit + S/P amplitude ratio misfit

    Note: das_sp alone is not a valid mode — S/P ratios must always be combined with polarity data. Similarly, sta_sp requires sta_pol.

    2. Load Ray Parameters and Observations for inversion¶

    We load pre-computed ray parameters (takeoff angle, azimuth, and distance) for both DAS channels and conventional stations (from lab3a), and match them with the corresponding observations.

    In [35]:
    Copied! 
    import h5py
from dasfm.io.data import RayParamTable
from dasfm.io.sta_io import load_sta_polarity, load_sta_sp_ratio

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load ray parameters
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# DAS ray parameters
das_table = RayParamTable.from_hdf5(RAY_PARAMS_DIR / f"table_das_{FORWARD_METHOD}.h5")
src_das = das_table.trial(0) if das_table.is_perturbed else das_table

# Station ray parameters
sta_table = RayParamTable.from_hdf5(RAY_PARAMS_DIR / f"table_sta_{FORWARD_METHOD}.h5")
src_sta = sta_table.trial(0) if sta_table.is_perturbed else sta_table
sta_stations = [str(s) for s in src_sta.station]
print(f"STA ray params: takeoff {src_sta.takeoff.shape}  stations={len(sta_stations)}")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load DAS observations
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# DAS polarity
with h5py.File(DAS_POL, "r") as f:
    Pkic = f["Pkic"][:]
    pol_event_ids = list(f["event_ids"].asstr()[:])

n_ch, _ = Pkic.shape
das_event_ids = [str(e) for e in pol_event_ids]
print(f"DAS polarity: {Pkic.shape}")

# DAS S/P ratios
with h5py.File(DAS_SP, "r") as f:
    sp_ratios = f["sp_ratios"][:].copy()
    sp_valid = f["sp_valid"][:]
    sp_ratios[~sp_valid] = np.nan

print(f"DAS S/P ratios: {sp_ratios.shape}")

# Match DAS ray parameters to the event order in DAS observations
src_eid_to_row = {str(eid): i for i, eid in enumerate(all_event_ids)}
ev_idx = np.array([src_eid_to_row[eid] for eid in das_event_ids])
ch_idx = np.arange(n_ch)

das_takeoff_deg = np.degrees(src_das.takeoff[np.ix_(ev_idx, ch_idx)]).astype(np.float32)
das_azimuth_deg = np.degrees(src_das.azimuth[np.ix_(ev_idx, ch_idx)]).astype(np.float32)
das_distance = src_das.raypath_length[np.ix_(ev_idx, ch_idx)]

print(f"DAS ray params: {das_takeoff_deg.shape}  (n_ev x n_ch)")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Load station observations
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
logger = code_Log()

# Station polarity observations
sta_pol_data = load_sta_polarity(STA_POL, STA_GEO, das_event_ids, all_event_ids, src_sta, logger)

# Station S/P ratio observations
sta_sp_data = load_sta_sp_ratio(STA_SP, das_event_ids, all_event_ids, src_sta, logger)

    3. Build SDR Grid¶

    Generate a uniform grid of strike, dip, and rake (SDR) angles to sample the focal mechanism space. Each grid point represents a candidate focal mechanism. The implementation here follows the grid construction strategy used in SKHASH.

    • Grid step — controls the angular resolution (default 5 degrees)
    • Uniform sampling — the number of azimuth points at each polar angle is proportional to sin(theta), ensuring approximately equal area per grid cell on the sphere
    • Moment tensor — each SDR triple is converted to a moment tensor for forward computation

    make_sdr_grid_skhash_style, sdr_to_mt, numpy_to_torch,
)

sdr_grid_dang_deg = 5.0
stk_g, dip_g, rak_g = make_sdr_grid_skhash_style(dang=sdr_grid_dang_deg)
stk_t = numpy_to_torch(stk_g, device=DEVICE)
dip_t = numpy_to_torch(dip_g, device=DEVICE)
rak_t = numpy_to_torch(rak_g, device=DEVICE)
num_Mt = stk_g.shape[0]
M_g = sdr_to_mt(stk_g, dip_g, rak_g)
M_g_t = numpy_to_torch(M_g, device=DEVICE)
print(f"SDR grid: {num_Mt} focal mechanisms")

    4. Forward Modeling and Misfit Evaluation¶

    For each event, we compute the theoretical polarity and S/P amplitude ratios using the ray parameters and all candidate SDR moment tensors.

    • For station observations, we use Aki’s radiation pattern formulation.
    • For DAS observations, we use a strain-rate formulation based on the normal strain expression of Luo et al., extended here to a complete forward model.

    Misfit Definitions¶

    We then evaluate the misfit between observations and predictions for each data type.

    • STA polarity misfit — count of polarity disagreements at conventional stations

    • STA S/P misfit — residual between observed and predicted station S/P ratios

    • DAS polarity misfit — count of polarity disagreements across DAS channels

    • DAS S/P misfit — residual between observed and predicted log₁₀(S/P), computed using a chosen norm, with optional mean-alignment correction

    S/P Misfit Norm¶

    The S/P amplitude misfit can be computed with different norms:

    • "L1" (default): sum(|x|) — Robust to outliers, each bad channel contributes linearly
    • "L2": sqrt(sum(x^2)) — Sensitive to large residuals, one bad channel can dominate
    • "cauchy": sum(log(1 + (x/c)^2)) — A smooth robust loss that lies between L1 and L2 norms, reducing the influence of large residuals while preserving sensitivity to moderate misfits. The scale parameter c = 2*sigma is estimated from the spatial noise level of the observed S/P ratios (median filter with window=200 channels, MAD-based sigma estimation)
    In [37]:
    Copied! 
    from dasfm.inversion.forward_model import compute_das_forward, compute_das_polarity_misfit_torch
from dasfm.inversion.filter import filter_pol_only, filter_joint, build_solution
from dasfm.inversion.cluster import cluster_solution_nooverlap
from dasfm.utils.step_utils import build_obs
from dasfm.inversion import cal_stdr


# Define event for demo
iev = 0
eid = das_event_ids[iev]
print(f"Event: {eid}")

# Observed polarity and S/P — torch tensors for the DAS forward model
pol_obs = torch.sign(torch.tensor(Pkic[:, iev], dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE))
sp_obs_das = torch.tensor(sp_ratios[:, iev], dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
# numpy copy for downstream filter / cal_stdr (both are numpy-only)
pol_obs_np = pol_obs.cpu().numpy()

# STA polarity forward (numpy)
sta_pol_misfits = []
sta_pol_i = None; sta_toa_deg_t0 = sta_az_deg_t0 = None; n_sta = 0
if sta_pol_data is not None and eid in sta_pol_data["eid_to_idx"]:
    sidx = sta_pol_data["eid_to_idx"][eid]
    sta_pol_i = sta_pol_data["polarities"][sidx]
    n_sta = len(sta_pol_i)
    sta_toa_deg_t0 = sta_pol_data["takeoffs"][sidx]
    sta_az_deg_t0 = sta_pol_data["azimuths"][sidx]
    toa_t = torch.tensor(sta_toa_deg_t0, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
    az_t = torch.tensor(sta_az_deg_t0, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
    pol_t = torch.tensor(sta_pol_i, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
    misfit = compute_sta_pol_misfit_torch(stk_t, dip_t, rak_t, toa_t, az_t, pol_t).cpu().numpy()
    sta_pol_misfits.append(misfit.astype(np.float32))
    print(f"  STA polarity misfit: min={misfit.min():.2f}, n_sta={n_sta}")

# STA S/P forward (numpy)
sta_sp_misfits = []; sta_sp_obs_i = None; sta_sp_toa_t0 = sta_sp_az_t0 = None; n_sta_sp = 0
if sta_sp_data is not None and eid in sta_sp_data["eid_to_idx"]:
    sp_sidx = sta_sp_data["eid_to_idx"][eid]
    sta_sp_obs_i = sta_sp_data["ratios"][sp_sidx]
    n_sta_sp = len(sta_sp_obs_i)
    sta_sp_toa_t0 = sta_sp_data["takeoffs"][sp_sidx]
    sta_sp_az_t0 = sta_sp_data["azimuths"][sp_sidx]
    toa_sp_t = torch.tensor(sta_sp_toa_t0, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
    az_sp_t = torch.tensor(sta_sp_az_t0, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
    sp_theo = compute_sta_sp_theo_torch(stk_t, dip_t, rak_t, toa_sp_t, az_sp_t).cpu().numpy()
    sta_sp_misfits.append(np.sum(np.abs(sp_theo - sta_sp_obs_i), axis=1).astype(np.float32))
    print(f"  STA S/P misfit:      min={sta_sp_misfits[0].min():.2f}, n_sta_sp={n_sta_sp}")


# DAS forward — polarity (Aki-Richards particle velocity, matches Pkic convention)
#                + amplitude/SP (strain rate, DAS physics)
m_pol = compute_das_polarity_misfit_torch(
    stk_t, dip_t, rak_t,
    das_takeoff_deg[iev], das_azimuth_deg[iev],
    pol_obs,
)
m_sp, corr = compute_das_forward(
    M_g_t, das_takeoff_deg[iev], das_azimuth_deg[iev],
    sp_obs_das=sp_obs_das,

    5. Inversion and Solution Clustering¶

    The inversion consists of three steps: thresholding, two-stage relaxation, and clustering of acceptable solutions.

    Key Inversion Parameters¶

    • init_pol_error — polarity buffer added to min misfit (default 0.02); threshold = min_misfit + pol_weighted × init_pol_error, relaxed if fewer solutions are found
    • init_amp_error_perc — percentile (default 0.5%) used to define the initial S/P amplitude misfit threshold
    • das_pol_weight — relative weight of DAS polarity compared to station polarity (range 0–1) in combined modes
    • joint_pol_size — in joint modes, minimum number of polarity-acceptable mechanisms before applying the amplitude filter (default 60)

    Initial Thresholding¶

    For each SDR candidate, polarity and (if applicable) S/P misfits are evaluated.

    • Polarity threshold — defined relative to the minimum misfit and scaled by the total polarity weight
    • S/P threshold (joint modes) — selected from the lower percentile of misfit values within the polarity-acceptable pool

    This step defines an initial set of acceptable solutions.

    Two-Stage Threshold Relaxation (Joint Modes)¶

    Polarity and S/P amplitude have different reliability and are treated in two explicit stages:

    • Stage 1 — Polarity pool: Relax the polarity threshold until at least joint_pol_size (default 60) mechanisms pass. This establishes a robust polarity-acceptable pool.
    • Stage 2 — Amplitude filter: Within the polarity pool, relax the S/P amplitude threshold until at least 20 mechanisms pass both criteria.

    Polarity is always prioritized — the amplitude filter only operates within the polarity-acceptable set. For polarity-only modes, only Stage 1 is used.

    Clustering and Refinement¶

    Accepted solutions are grouped and refined using hierarchical clustering in Kagan-angle space.

    • Cluster solutions using a 45° distance threshold
    • Compute a weighted average focal mechanism for each cluster
    • Iteratively refine and remove outliers using a stricter (~30°) criterion

    Each cluster yields one candidate solution, characterized by its mean mechanism, misfit, uncertainty, and acceptance ratio.

    Final solutions are ranked by acceptance ratio, and up to five candidates are retained.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = 150

# Polarity buffer: thresh = min_misfit + pol_weighted * init_pol_error
init_pol_error = 0.02       

# Initial S/P amplitude error percentile
init_amp_error_perc = 0.005  

# DAS vs STA polarity weight in combined modes (0-1)
das_pol_weight = 0.5         

# In joint modes, polarity pool size before amplitude filter
joint_pol_size = 60  
      

das_sum = float(np.abs(pol_obs_np).sum())

def build_obs_for_mode(mode):
    return build_obs(mode, iev, n_ch, Pkic,
                      [np.degrees(src_das.takeoff)], [np.degrees(src_das.azimuth)],
                      sp_ratios, sta_toa_deg_t0, sta_az_deg_t0, sta_pol_i,
                      sta_sp_toa_t0, sta_sp_az_t0, sta_sp_obs_i, True)


repr_ctx = dict(
    device=DEVICE, n_ch=n_ch,
    das_pol_weight=das_pol_weight,
    do_mean_alignment=True,
    sp_norm="L1", cauchy_c=None,
    NMC=1,
)

def invert_mode(mode, pol_misfits, amp_misfits, pol_weighted, n_measure):
    """Filter -> cluster -> compute_representatives for one mode."""
    pol_stack = np.stack(pol_misfits)  # (1, num_Mt)
    amp_stack = None
    if amp_misfits and any(m is not None for m in amp_misfits):
        amp_stack = np.stack([m for m in amp_misfits if m is not None])
    if amp_stack is not None:
        mask = filter_joint(pol_stack, amp_stack, pol_weighted,
                             init_pol_error, init_amp_error_perc,
                             joint_pol_size=joint_pol_size)
    else:
        mask = filter_pol_only(pol_stack, pol_weighted, init_pol_error)
    sol = build_solution(mask, pol_stack, amp_stack, pol_weighted,
                          stk_g, dip_g, rak_g, n_measure)
    if sol is None:
        return [], []
    cand = cluster_solution_nooverlap(sol)
    if cand:
        spec = MODE_REGISTRY[mode]
        compute_representatives(spec, cand, fwd_misfits, event_obs, repr_ctx)
    return sol, cand

print(f"Event: {eid}")

    6. Production: Invert All Events¶

    The cells above demonstrated the inversion pipeline on a single event. To produce focal mechanisms for all 25 events × 7 modes (written to result_try1/ for lab 3d), call the production step3_invert function.
